## Recap of confidence intervals

### Exercise 1: 

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**a.** Write a function called `mean_CI` that takes parameters `x` (a numeric vector) and `alpha` (a significance level) and outputs a closed confidence interval as a vector.

:::

```{r Q1a}
#' Required variables: mean_CI (function)
#' Required plots: 

# Your function declaration should look somewhat like
# mean_CI <- function(x, alpha) {
# ... function contents here ...
# }

# Solution
mean_CI <- function(x, alpha) {
  N <- length(x)
  mean(x) + qt(c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2), N - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(N)
}

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**b.** Build your data frame following the instructions in the assignment specs and store it as a data frame called `sim_CI`. 
:::

```{r Q1b}
#' Required variables: sim_CI (data.frame)
#' Required plots: 
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)})
set.seed(1234567)

nreps <- 50
# Initialising the dataframe for you:
sim_CI <- data.frame(replicate = 1:nreps,
                     xbar = rep(NA, nreps), 
                     CI_l = rep(NA, nreps), 
                     CI_u = rep(NA, nreps))

# Enter your solution here
# (...)

# Solution
for (i in 1:nreps){
  x <- rnorm(30, 10, 15)
  CI <- mean_CI(x, 0.05)
  sim_CI$xbar[i] <- mean(x)
  sim_CI[i, 3:4] <- CI
}
```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**c.** Add the required new column to your dataset. It may be useful to use `ifelse()` and the logical AND, `&`
:::

```{r Q1c}
#' Required variables: sim_CI (data.frame)
#' Required plots: 

sim_CI$captures <- ifelse(sim_CI$CI_l <= 10 & sim_CI$CI_u >= 10,
                          TRUE, FALSE)
```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**d.**  Generate the plot as specified in the assignment specs.
:::

```{r Q1d}
#' Required variables: 
#' Required plots: TRUE

ggplot(sim_CI, aes(x = xbar, y = replicate, 
                   xmax = CI_u, xmin = CI_l, 
                   colour = captures)) + 
  geom_pointrange() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() + labs(title = "50 confidence intervals", x = "x")

```

### Exercise 2: 

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**a.** Modify your confidence interval function from Exercise 1 to also be able to calculate one-sided intervals, as indicated in the Assignment specs. 
:::


```{r Q2a}
#' Required variables: mean_CI2 (function)
#' Required plots: 

# Your function declaration should look somewhat like
# mean_CI2 <- function(x, alpha, type) {
# ... function contents here ...
# }

# Solution
mean_CI2 <- function(x, alpha, type) {
  N <- length(x)
  
  if (type == "lower"){
    mean(x) + qt(alpha, N - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(N)
  } else if (type == "upper"){
    mean(x) + qt(1 - alpha, N - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(N)
  } else if (type == "two.sided"){
    mean(x) + qt(c(alpha/2, 1 - alpha/2), N - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(N)
  } else {
    stop("type not recognised. Please use 'lower', 'upper' or 'two.sided'")
  }
}

```


### Exercise 3: 

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**a.** Read the data in file `pharma_drug_spending.csv` into a data frame called `oecd.pharma`. 
:::


```{r Q3a}
#' Required variables: oecd.pharma (data.frame)
#' Required plots: 

# Solution
oecd.pharma <- read.csv("./pharma_drug_spending.csv", header = TRUE)

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**b.** Create the summary data frame as specified in the assignment specs.
:::


```{r Q3b}
#' Required variables: perc.per.year (data.frame)
#' Required plots: 

# Solution
alpha <- 0.05
perc.per.year <- oecd.pharma %>%
  group_by(TIME) %>%
  summarise(mean_PC_GDP = mean(PC_GDP),
            N           = n(),
            CI_L        = mean_CI2(PC_GDP, alpha = 2*alpha, type = "lower"),
            CI_U        = mean_CI2(PC_GDP, alpha = 2*alpha, type = "upper")) %>%
  filter(TIME >= 1970, TIME <= 2020)

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**c.** Create the plot with the mean % GDP / year and their respective confidence intervals.
:::

```{r Q3c}
#' Required variables: 
#' Required plots: TRUE

# Solution

## Basic plot
ggplot(perc.per.year, aes(x = TIME, y = mean_PC_GDP)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = CI_L, ymax = CI_U))

## A more sophisticated plot
ggplot(perc.per.year, aes(x = TIME, y = mean_PC_GDP)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = CI_L, ymax = CI_U)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2003, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 2002.5, y = 1.7, 
           label = "2003", colour = "red", hjust = 1) + 
  labs(title = "Mean % GDP spent on pharma drugs per year", 
       caption = "Source: OECD, DataHub", 
       x = "Year", y = "% GDP") + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())
```

### Exercise 4

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**a.** Generate a random vector called `x` containing 30 observations drawn from a normal distribution with $\mu = 100$ and $\sigma^2 = 144$. (Notice that you have the _variance_, but function `rnorm()` expects the _standard deviation_). Use the data in this vector to validate your function `mean_CI2()`, checking that it returns the same confidence limits as `t.test()` for two-sided, lower and upper confidence limits.

:::

```{r Q4a}
#' Required variables: x (numeric)
#' Required plots: 

# Solution
x <- rnorm(30, mean = 100, sd = sqrt(144))

# Testing 2-sided interval
mean_CI2(x, alpha = 0.05, type = "two.sided")
t.test(x, conf.level = 0.95, alternative = "two.sided")$conf.int

# Testing upper confidence bound
mean_CI2(x, alpha = 0.01, type = "upper")
t.test(x, conf.level = 0.99, alternative = "less")$conf.int

# Testing lower confidence bound
mean_CI2(x, alpha = 0.02, type = "lower")
t.test(x, conf.level = 0.98, alternative = "greater")$conf.int
```

```{r Q5c}
#' Required variables: Y (data.frame)
#' Required plots: FALSE

Y <- NHANES %>%
  filter(Gender == "female",
         Age >= 30,
         Race1 %in% c("Black", "Hispanic"),
         Education == "College Grad",
         !is.na(BPSysAve))

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**d.** Calculate the individual confidence intervals and plot them.

:::

```{r Q5d}
#' Required variables: CIs_1 (data.frame)
#' Required plots: TRUE

# Solution
CIs_1 <- Y %>%
  rename(Population = Race1) %>%
  group_by(Population) %>%
  summarise(est  = mean(BPSysAve),
            CI_L = t.test(BPSysAve, conf.level = 0.95)$conf.int[1],
            CI_U = t.test(BPSysAve, conf.level = 0.95)$conf.int[2])

ggplot(CIs_1, aes(x = est, y = Population)) + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = CI_L, xmax = CI_U)) + 
  theme_light() + 
  labs(title = "Confidence intervals on mean systolic blood pressure",
       subtitle = "College-educated women in the U.S., aged 30 and over",
       caption = "Source: NHANES",
       x = "Combined systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)") + 
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**e.** Calculate the confidence interval on the difference of the two means and add it to the 'CIs_1' dataframe.

:::

```{r Q5e}
#' Required variables: CIs_1
#' Required plots: 

# Solution
x.bl <- Y %>%
  filter(Race1 == "Black") %>% 
  pull(BPSysAve)

x.hs <- Y %>%
  filter(Race1 == "Hispanic") %>% 
  pull(BPSysAve)

CIs_1 <- rbind(CIs_1,
               data.frame(
                 Population = "Black - Hispanic",
                 est = mean(x.bl) - mean(x.hs),
                 CI_L = t.test(x = x.bl, y = x.hs, conf.level = 0.95, var.equal = FALSE)$conf.int[1],
                 CI_U = t.test(x = x.bl, y = x.hs, conf.level = 0.95, var.equal = FALSE)$conf.int[2]))

CIs_1

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**f.** Add the confidence interval half-widths to the `CIs_1` dataframe.

:::

```{r Q5f}
#' Required variables: CIs_1
#' Required plots: 

# Solution
CIs_1 <- CIs_1 %>%
  mutate(CIhw = (CI_U - CI_L) / 2)

CIs_1
```


### Exercise 6:

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**a.** Build the function `median_ci_boot` as indicated in the CW specs
:::

```{r Q6a}
#' Required variables: median_ci_boot (function)
#' Required plots: 

median_ci_boot <- function(x, R, conf){
  alpha = 1 - conf
  boot_medians <- replicate(R, median(sample(x, size = length(x), replace = TRUE)))
  quantile(boot_medians, c(alpha / 2, 1 - alpha / 2))
}

```

:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**b.** Calculate the confidence interval as indicated in the assignment specs.
:::

```{r Q6b}
#' Required variables: med_usd_cap_ci (numeric)
#' Required plots: 

# Reload the data
oecd.pharma <- read.csv("./pharma_drug_spending.csv", header = TRUE)

med_usd_cap_ci <- oecd.pharma %>%
  filter(TIME == 2020) %>%
  pull(USD_CAP) %>%
  median_ci_boot(R = 2000, conf = 0.95)

```


:::{#prompt .message style="color: blue;"}
**c.** Calculate the mean and $95\%$ CI on the median %GDP spent per year on pharmaceutical drugs in OECD countries, and generate the plot as indicated in the assignment specs. 
:::

```{r Q6c}
#' Required variables: 
#' Required plots: TRUE
library (tidyr)
myCIs <- oecd.pharma %>%
  filter(TIME >= 1980, TIME <= 2020) %>%
  group_by(TIME) %>%
  summarise(Med = median(PC_GDP),
            CI  = list(median_ci_boot(PC_GDP, R = 1000, conf = 0.95))) %>%
  unnest_wider(CI) %>%
  rename(CI_L = `2.5%`,
         CI_U = `97.5%`)

ggplot(myCIs, aes(x = TIME, y = Med, ymin = CI_L, ymax = CI_U)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = CI_L, ymax = CI_U)) +
  labs(title = "Median % GDP spent on pharma drugs per year", 
       subtitle = "OECD countries",
       caption = "Source: OECD, DataHub", 
       x = "Year", y = "% GDP") + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

```
